subject: general
question: A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. In how many years it will becomes five times of itself?
solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the interest rate be R%.

​According to the question,

(P × R × 26)/100 = 3P - P

⇒ (P × R × 26)/100 = 2P

⇒ R = 100/13

Let's suppose, it will take T years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.

​According to the question,

(P × 100/13 × T)/100 = (5P - P)

⇒ T = 13 × 4

⇒ T = 52

∴ it will take 52 years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.
